headline: Thin Black Friday half-day after a volatile Nvidia-led week; futures headlines point up

what_happened.summary: The Cboe Daily Take (25 Nov) says stocks opened in a deep Nvidia-led selloff and dip buyers pulled them off the lows. The Nasdaq-100 briefly touched bear-market territory intraday. Cboe names hotter inflation data, renewed tariff concerns and Nvidia credit-rating actions as pressures. US markets were closed on Thursday for the holiday. Cboe warns that today's half-day session will be thin and can exaggerate moves.
what_happened.market_action: FRED shows the Nasdaq-100 closed at 26046.9 (-0.64%) on 25 Nov. Cboe says the S&P 500 fell as much as 3.21% intraday and closed 0.35% lower, and the Dow closed up 0.33%. The VIX table lists 26.8 (-5.27%) dated 26 Nov, a day US equities were closed, so treat it with care. VXN was 38.53, VVIX 115.38 and COR1M 25.45 on 25 Nov.
what_happened.macro: Core PCE rose 3.3% y/y per Cboe (FRED: 3.26% y/y, 0.29% m/m), up from 3.1% in September. The 10-year yield fell to 4.85% (-6.0 bp) on 25 Nov per Treasury. Polymarket prices a 25 bp December hike at 94.5%, and Cboe cites CME FedWatch at 59% for another 25 bp hike in January, down from 70% a week earlier.
what_happened.geopolitics: Not covered by the sources. Oil data is stale to 24 Nov: Brent 91.8, WTI 82.24.
what_happened.company_news: S&P Global Ratings put Nvidia's senior unsecured debt on CreditWatch negative, citing management and governance, board independence and key-man risk. Cboe says Moody's cut Nvidia's outlook from positive to stable last week. Nvidia closed 3.9% lower and Anthropic closed 1.08% higher after falling nearly 10% intraday. Cboe lists early-December House hearings among open Nvidia issues.

unconfirmed: Headlines say US stock futures are rising on Black Friday, with Nasdaq futures leading and S&P 500 futures topping 7,300.
Headlines say Nvidia and Anthropic are rallying in premarket after earlier AI selloff.
Headlines on Treasuries conflict: one says yields rise, another says Treasuries retreat as equities gain. Another headline reports an Iran-linked drone attack in Kuwait.
driver_reason: Nvidia drove both the selloff and the dip-buying on 25 Nov, and the credit-rating actions keep governance risk open. Hot core PCE and a priced December hike add pressure, but the day's swings tracked Nvidia and AI names.
leader_reason: The Nasdaq-100 trailed the S&P 500 by 1.49 pct pts on 24 Nov and by 1.02 pct pts over 5 sessions. VXN at 38.53 sits well above VIX at 28.29 on 25 Nov, and COR1M at 25.45 is elevated. Tech and the AI complex are setting the tone.

S&P put Nvidia debt on CreditWatch negative and Moody's cut the outlook. Core PCE 3.26% y/y per FRED. The 10-year yield is 4.85%. VXN 38.53, VIX 28.29, COR1M 25.45. A December hike is priced (Polymarket 94.5%), January odds 59% per CME per Cboe. US was closed on 26 Nov and 27 Nov is a thin half-day. Premarket headlines (unverified) show futures rising. Jobs data on 1 and 4 Dec lead into the 9 Dec FOMC.
